title: Reactive vs Proactive Autoscaling Comparison — Regional GPU Capacity
summary: Working sheet comparing reactive (threshold-based) autoscaling to proactive (forecast-driven) approaches across three regions. Goal: quantify latency, cost, and stability tradeoffs and recommend min/max and trigger settings for Dedicated fleet targets.
objectives: 1) Measure tail latency and scale stabilization for reactive vs proactive. 2) Produce actionable min/max and cooldown recommendations per region. 3) Identify metrics to drive hybrid mode (when to pre-warm).
assumptions:
- Traffic patterns used are from production-sampled traces (Jul 2026).
- Model footprint = 80GB GPU memory per replica for r-infer-v2.
- Start/attach time for new GPU repl = 95s average (cold), warm spin-up using reserved cache ~ 18s.
- Billing granularity: per-minute.
- Autoscaler supports predictive signal (forecast) and standard thresholds; can set separate min/max per region.
methodology: Run 72-hour controlled runs per region: 24h baseline reactive, 24h proactive, 24h hybrid. Injected synthetic surges of +3x sustained for 6-12 minutes at random times to emulate traffic spikes. Collected: 95th/99th gen latency, average GPU utilization, scale actions, cost proxy (GPU-minutes), and incidents (missed SLOs).
experiment-parameters:
Reactive config baseline: min=8, max=160, scale_up_threshold=70% averaged over 30s, scale_down_threshold=40% over 120s, cool_down_up=120s, cool_down_down=300s, scale_step=+8.
Proactive config baseline: min=8, max=160, forecast_horizon=180s, forecast_confidence=0.8, warm_pool=12 (reserved), pre-warm_trigger=predicted_peak>current_pool*1.2.
Hybrid: reactive primary, allow forecast to pre-warm only when predicted surge > 20% and duration>90s.

key_findings:
- Proactive scaling consistently reduces tail latency (95p and 99p) by ~20–35% compared to reactive at the cost of ~6–12% more GPU-minutes (depends on region).
- Reactive schemes experienced oscillation when surges appear back-to-back; large scale_step (+8) caused overprovisioning followed by long cooldowns.
- Warm-pool + pre-warm reduces cold start penalty (spin-up from warm ~18s vs cold ~95s). Regions with higher variance (ap-southeast1) see the largest incident delta if reactive-only.
- Hybrid mode gave the best balance in us-west1 and ap-southeast1: minimal extra cost (approx +4%) with most cold starts eliminated.
recommendations:
1) Adopt hybrid autoscaling as default for Dedicated fleets with region-specific knobs.
2) Region defaults: us-west1 min=8 max=160 scale_step=+6 down_step=-6; eu-west1 min=6 max=120 scale_step=+4; ap-southeast1 min=4 max=80 scale_step=+4.
3) Reactive thresholds: scale_up=70%, scale_down=40%, up_cooldown=90s, down_cooldown=240s (shorter up cooldown than baseline to reduce 99p latency).
4) Proactive config: forecast_horizon=180s, warm_pool size = 15% of max (subject to cost cap), pre-warm trigger confidence=0.75.
5) Implement a back-to-back surge protection: cap scale_step growth if >2 scale events in 10m to avoid overshoot.
6) Add an "emergency fast path" for tiny hot queues: allow ephemeral micro-bursts via pre-warmed n1s GPUs when predicted surge <60s to avoid full replica startup for short spikes.
risks_and_open_questions:
- Forecast false positives increase cost; need to calibrate confidence thresholds regionally.
- Billing granularity may cause higher-than-expected customer cost in per-minute billing for many short pre-warms.
- Does metric aggregation window (30s) hide micro-burst that matters for tail latency? We should test 10s windows.
- Need SRE review of warm_pool security/tenant isolation.
- Can we get faster attach times via infra changes (container keep-alive, persistent KV caches)?
follow_ups:

- Avoid changing min values mid-pilot; test within canary cohorts.
- Check with sales on committed capacity impacts if we increase warm_pool allocations for Dedicated accounts.
conclusion: Hybrid (reactive + selective forecasting) is the recommended path: materially better tail latency and stability with modest cost delta. Next step is a controlled production pilot with 10s telemetry and conservative warm_pool sizing.
